title: Astrid and the Ember
premise: Wendell Iversen, a storm-caller exiled for refusing to weaponize his gift, has spent fifteen years guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains, hiding from the gods he blames for his sister's death. When the old gods stir and prayers begin to be answered, Wendell learns his late sister's soul was sold to the Ember Court beneath the mountain by the very priests who exiled him—and that her soul is the final ember needed to reignite their dying god. With a runaway shrine-keeper named Astrid, who can hear the mountain speaking, Wendell descends through smuggler roads into the court itself. He bargains, fights, and finally offers his own storm-gift in trade, breaking his exile at last; Astrid inherits both the shrine and the found family they gathered along the way, while Wendell's sister passes on free, leaving him belonging among the living.
about_author: Mirabel Ishikawa is a former cartographer of alpine trails who now writes fantasy from a cabin full of hand-drawn maps of places that don't exist. Her work explores what people inherit when bloodlines fail them.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell guides a smuggling caravan through Thornfell, demonstrating his uncanny knowledge of hidden passes while dodging questions about his past. A tremor in the stone—impossible, since the mountain has been silent for decades—rattles him. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness, ending with the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Astrid of the Cold Shrine
chapters.summary: Astrid, a sixteen-year-old shrine-keeper abandoned when her temple's god went quiet, hears the mountain speak her name and flees her village before the frightened elders can silence her. She stows away in Wendell's caravan. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terror transforming into stubborn hope as she chooses the unknown over a hollow home.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: In the border town of Greymoss, old shrines flicker alight overnight and desperate pilgrims flood in—but some answered prayers come back wrong, twisted by something beneath the mountain. Wendell recognizes the pattern: the Ember Court is feeding again. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant recognition that his exile's peace is over.

chapters.title: What the Priests Sold
chapters.summary: A dying priest confesses to Wendell that fifteen years ago the Ember Court bought souls to sustain its fading god—among them, Wendell's sister Solveig, taken after the exile that killed her body but not her soul. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: grief detonating into fury; the revelation reframes everything he believed about his sister's death.

chapters.title: Three Companions on a Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Wendell, Astrid, and Bramble—a disgraced caravan guard who owes Wendell a debt—travel toward the deep passes. Astrid's growing ability to hear the mountain saves them from a collapsing road, earning Wendell's grudging trust. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: found family forming around campfires, warmth Wendell resists and Astrid insists upon.

chapters.title: The Toll Gate of Names
chapters.summary: At the mountain's threshold, a gate demands each traveler surrender a true name or a true memory. Astrid gives up her memory of her mother; Wendell nearly gives up his name—the anchor of his identity—before Bramble sacrifices instead. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: guilt and awe, realizing others will pay prices he's been hoarding his whole life.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: They descend into the Ember Court, a cathedral of banked fires where soul-lanterns hang like fruit. Wendell finds Solveig's lantern dimming—the ember-harvest approaches. The Court's herald offers him a bargain: serve the dying god willingly, and Solveig lives on as its vessel. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy, testing whether love means keeping someone or freeing them.

chapters.title: The Harvest of Embers
chapters.summary: Refusing the bargain, Wendell and Astrid attempt to steal Solveig's lantern during the harvest ceremony. The Court awakens its half-born god; Bramble falls holding the escape route open, and Astrid is captured when she refuses to leave without the other stolen souls. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: sacrifice and capture, courage curdling into despair as the plan collapses.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Deep
chapters.summary: To save Astrid and the lanterns, Wendell does what exile forbade: he calls the storm, channeling lightning down the mountain's throat into the starving god—not to feed it, but to shatter it, releasing every soul it held. He offers his own gift as payment. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: climax; self-destruction transmuted into liberation, the exile finally spending himself for others.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: The Court crumbles; the freed souls disperse like sparks. Solveig appears briefly to forgive Wendell before passing on. Astrid, hearing the mountain offer her the emptied shrine as a living hearth, accepts—and names Wendell and the recovering Bramble her family. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: resolution; grief settled into peace, inheritance redefined as belonging freely chosen.
